story.title: From Sohar to Global Markets: How Oman Is Building an Integrated Pharmaceutical Manufacturing Hub

detail.extracted_title: From Sohar to Global Markets: How Oman Is Building an Integrated Pharmaceutical Manufacturing Hub
detail.excerpt: Anchored by three specialized industrial ventures in Sohar—Al Wajar Pharmaceuticals, Drug Manufacturing Company (DMC), and Penicillin Integrated Industries (Pen-G)—the Sultanate is expanding from finished formulations into active pharmaceutical ingredients and antibiotic raw materials for world markets.
detail.article_html:
In the industrial corridors of Sohar in North Al Batinah Governorate, a specialized cluster of chemical and medical plants is changing how the Sultanate participates in global healthcare. Rather than relying solely on importing finished medicines or packaging basic formulations, Oman is building an upstream pharmaceutical manufacturing base capable of producing advanced drug pellets, active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs), and core raw materials for life-saving antibiotics.

Anchored by three complementary industrial ventures in Sohar—Al Wajar Pharmaceuticals, Drug Manufacturing Company (DMC), and Penicillin Integrated Industries (Pen-G)—and reinforced by new academic partnerships to train Omani pharmacists in industrial production, the sector has become a practical pillar of non-oil export diversification under Oman Vision 2040.

Al Wajar Pharmaceuticals: Exporting 100 Percent of Production Across Four Regions

Operating in Sohar since 2018, Al Wajar Pharmaceuticals has demonstrated that Omani-manufactured medical products can compete directly in regulated international markets. Focusing on high-precision pharmaceutical pellets and specialized drug delivery formulations, the company has developed more than 18 specialized products since launching operations.

Today, Al Wajar exports 100 percent of its output to international markets across Asia, Africa, Latin America, and the Middle East. Its trajectory offers a clear working model for how specialized industrial manufacturing in North Al Batinah can generate high-value non-oil exports while establishing an Omani quality benchmark abroad.

Localizing the Supply Chain: Drug Manufacturing Company and Pen-G Antibiotics

While finished and semi-finished formulations open export doors, global supply shocks in recent years have underscored the strategic importance of controlling raw pharmaceutical inputs. Two major industrial projects in Sohar are addressing that gap directly across the production chain.

Drug Manufacturing Company (DMC) is establishing advanced industrial infrastructure designed to supply regional pharmaceutical plants with essential Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients (APIs). By producing the biologically active compounds that make medicines work, DMC strengthens local and Gulf supply chain security while retaining higher industrial value inside the Sultanate.

Beside it, Penicillin Integrated Industries (Pen-G) is targeting the foundational raw materials required to manufacture penicillin and related antibiotics. Engineered for large-scale global export, the Pen-G project is positioning Omani-made antibiotic raw materials to supply major international healthcare markets, led by the United States market, while attracting advanced foreign pharmaceutical investment and technology transfer to North Al Batinah.

Preparing Omani Talent for Industrial Pharmacy

Building chemical reactors and cleanroom production lines requires a parallel investment in specialized national talent. To connect classroom pharmacy education with factory-floor innovation, the Oman College of Health Sciences recently signed a memorandum of understanding with Indonesia's Padjadjaran University during a joint academic visit in Bali from November 3 to 5, 2026.

Signed by Dr. Fahad bin Mahmoud Al Zadjali, Dean of the Oman College of Health Sciences, alongside Dr. Abdullah bin Ali Al Balushi, Director of the Pharmacy Program, the five-year agreement focuses directly on training Omani students and faculty in industrial pharmaceutical manufacturing, drug discovery, and pharmaceutical technology. Through joint laboratory exchanges and specialized industrial training, the partnership ensures that as Sohar's API and antibiotic plants scale up, a new generation of Omani pharmaceutical scientists and engineers is ready to lead them.

detail.instagram_caption:
In the industrial corridors of Sohar in North Al Batinah Governorate, Oman is building a full-scale pharmaceutical manufacturing chain that reaches from advanced drug pellets to active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs) and raw materials for life-saving antibiotics.

Three complementary industrial projects in Sohar anchor this expansion. Operating since 2018, Al Wajar Pharmaceuticals has developed more than 18 high-precision specialized products and exports 100 percent of its output to markets across Asia, Africa, Latin America, and the Middle East.

Alongside it, Drug Manufacturing Company (DMC) is building industrial infrastructure to supply regional factories with essential Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients, strengthening medical supply security across the Gulf. Meanwhile, Penicillin Integrated Industries (Pen-G) is producing core raw materials for antibiotics aimed at major global healthcare markets, led by the United States.

To ensure national talent leads this industrial growth, the Oman College of Health Sciences—represented by Dean Dr. Fahad bin Mahmoud Al Zadjali and Pharmacy Program Director Dr. Abdullah bin Ali Al Balushi—recently signed a five-year partnership with Indonesia's Padjadjaran University to train Omani pharmacy students and researchers in industrial drug manufacturing and pharmaceutical technology.
